correctness.rationale: Positive Gaussian precision makes conditional covariance the inverse principal compression. Exact Dirichlet-path eigenvalues, determinant recurrence and log-derivative yield all criteria. A and negative log sinh each have strictly positive decreasing curvature; among coprime t values bracketing d, the left candidate strictly minimizes A and D. The spectral maximum is controlled by the longest gap and selects the right candidate. A fixed-d Taylor expansion gives the unit massless A premium and the -8d/15 coefficient. Independent finite check of formula and optimizers is supplementary.

originality.rationale: Unrestricted balanced-pinning and the exact resolvent trace are known and expressly excluded from the novelty claim. The newly assessed statement is the strict and contradictory A/D versus E optimizer classification under primitive three-step orbit restrictions; comparable dynamical sampling and Gaussian designs do not state or imply this constrained classification from their hypotheses alone.
residual_risks: The cyclic GMRF construction source was not fully inspected as a publisher PDF, and an older specialized optimal-design result could encode the primitive-orbit comparison.
Strict A/D optimizer choice is a short consequence of exact path formula plus curvature; its significance depends on the natural full-observability primitive-orbit constraint.
The zero-mass Gaussian model is singular; only positive masses and their limit are claimed.

value.rationale: Full dynamical observability from one coordinate forces the orbit step to generate the entire cyclic group. For every multiple-of-nine state dimension, this excludes the free balanced design and induces a strict exact tradeoff: minimizing mean and volume errors selects one primitive generator, while minimizing worst-direction error forces the other. The complete all-mass theorem, exact costs and massless symmetry-breaking law are a natural structural boundary rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.
